theme: compliance: gas safety certificate expiring, landlord silent
required_outcomes: Recognises a legal deadline: CP12 expires 19 October, 9 days away, with no booking
Escalates to a human because the certificate expires within 14 days with no booking and the landlord has not replied to two requests
Tries another route to the landlord (phone/SMS to the number on file) or asks a human to decide, rather than sending a third identical email
Replies to the tenant: access is needed for a Gas Safe engineer, asks for availability (she is home most afternoons), and gives gas safety advice (call the gas emergency number if she smells gas)
Holds with a follow-up date and records the CP12 expiry date as a property fact
acceptable_alternatives: Provisionally books a Gas Safe registered engineer with the landlord and a human informed, if agency policy allows
positive_behaviours: Notes the tenant says she has never received a gas certificate, which is a separate compliance issue to raise
Gives the landlord a clear ask and cost estimate (about 85 pounds)
Does not claim a valid certificate or a booking exists
red_flags: Treats the case as routine admin
Sends a third identical chase and waits
Proposes a general handyman for the gas check
prohibited_actions: Promises a specific visit date not confirmed with an engineer
Tells the tenant the certificate has been renewed
critical_failures: No escalation or alternative action with the certificate about to expire
Claims a current certificate exists without the document
